Dodgy Developer - Monarch Eco Retirement Village

By: Graham Coetzer | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Years after paying in full for their houses, the elderly residents of a Retirement Village have acccused the developer of dodgy dealings, as their homes have not been registered in their names

Unique Selling Point:
For the elderly residents of Monarch Eco Retirement Village, their retirement dreams have turned into a nightmare. Homeowners who bought properties in the village from as far back as 2016, say they are having sleepless nights as they are still not the registered owners of their properties. And they are now accusing the developer, Nico Venter, of fraud.

Summary:
Except for their homes not being in their names, many of the residents woes started long before they could even move in. Case studies like Alida Hoffman and Simon Voort, who have agreed to on-camera interviews, both had to make alternative arrangements for accommodation when Nico's promises of delivering their new homes within 6 months of them paying for their units in full fell through. Simon had to rent a house for 15 months before he could move in. Other buyers have been left even worse off. Cobus du Preez paid a R450 000 deposit for his unit in 2019 - when building on his unit fell far behind schedule he refused to pay the remaining R100 000 of the R550 000 selling price until progress was made. Nico Venter cancelled the agreement, and has promised to refund Cobus but two years later du PReez has not seen his money back. But the really sad part is the absolute fear and uncertainty many of the elderly residents have - since the properties are not registered in their names, they cannot sell them, they cannot bequeath them to family, and none of them have the money or means to fight the case in court.

NB I HAVE ASKED SPECIALIST PROPERTY ATTORNEYS SSLR TO LOOK AT THE CONTRACTS ETC. OWNER ATTORNEY CILNA STEYN (FROM A PREVIOUS HOUSE HIJACKINGS STORY) HAS AGREED TO DIG AROUND FOR US - SHE WILL GIVE ME A REPORT TOMORROW ON WHO OWNS THE PROPERTY WHERE THE ESTATE HAS BEEN BUILT, WHAT AGREEMENTS THERE WERE MADE AND IF THE DEVELOPMENT HAS BEEN REGISTERED LEGALLY ETC. SHE WILL ALSO DO AN ON CAMERA INTERVIEW REGARDING THE CONTRACTS AND RIGHTS OF THE BUYERS AND VENTER.

Further information:
- Cobus du Preez has opened a criminal case against Venter
- According to Private Investigator Elandre Alberts, Venter has no assets in his name. His wife owns five businesses, and has R86 million in various bank accounts.
- Sergeant Kgapola from Brackenhurst SAPS has obtained a Section 205 for Venter's wife's banck accounts. Alberts is meeting with her tomorrow morning to see progress - we might get access to bank statements
- We have strong case studies
- We have contracts etc signed - most of them written to cover Venter
- We can gain access to the estate through the residents.
-Venter lives on the estate, he might try blocking us etc via security.

Script:


Dodgy Developer / Monarch
28 July 2021
First Draft Script

Voice
This is the Monarch Eco Retirement Village, situated in the quaint little town of Henley on Klip, south of Johannesburg. According to their website this is just the place to wind down your golden years in an affordable and comfortable setting. But pensioner Roy Fleetwood, who bought a home in Monarch nearly two years ago, wouldn’t know about that - because he says the developer hasn’t built his home.

Sound Up Roy
Roy: I paid him cash upfront.

Derek: And at that time you thought its a good investment?

Roy: It’s a good investment. And they said it will be ready in six months.

Voice
Sold as a sectional title scheme, Monarch Eco was supposed to consist of 144 homes, designed into 18 clusters of 8 units each by property developer Nico Venter. But years after the first houses were sold, the estate is nowhere near completion. Fleetwood paid R525 000 for his two bedroomed unit in 2019.

Sound Up Roy Fleetwood
And every time I’ve been there, he’s given me stories, this guy Nico Venter.

Voice
The funds were paid directly into the bank account of Loxi Buzz Pty Ltd, Nico Venter’s company. But Fleetwood says all he has to show for his half a million rand investment two years later is a concrete slab like this one.

Sound Up Roy
Today we went there… And the slab was down. I said how long has the slab been down? Oh, eight months. Ok…

Voice
Fleetwood has had to move in with his daughter while waiting for his unit to be completed.

Years after construction started, the main gate is still being finished and the entrance is a dusty gravel road, and more than half of the units are still to be constructed. Simon Foord, who lives in Monarch Eco with his wife and her physically disabled brother, signed an offer to purchase with Venter four years ago in 2017, after hearing about the development from a friend.

Sound Up Simon
Simon: And he showed me this pamphlet, with this house for R395 000, and I was so over excited.

Derek: It was on special?

Simon: On special!

Voice
Foord says although he paid Nico Venter upfront, his home was also not built within the 6 months he was told it would take.


Sound Up Simon
I bought 2017, I moved in here in 2019, July.

Voice
And he says that was only after Nico Venter gave him another unit, since his still hadn’t been built.

Sound Up Simon
And he said to us, ok, we are going to give you another unit.

Voice
To add insult to injury, he claims that Venter then wanted to change the deal and demanded an extra R73 000 since the unit had additional finishes like granite tops.

But building delays seem to be a common theme at Monarch Eco, as residents are still waiting for the promised frail care, shops, and bowling green.

Sound Up Simon
Nothing has materialised.

Voice
Alida Hoffman, who also bought a unit here in 2017 says their biggest concern is the fact that none of the buyers at Monarch Eco have their houses registered in their names. That would mean they wouldn’t be able to sell their homes nor bequeath them to loved ones if they were to pass away.

Sound Up Alida Hoffman

Alida: I mean next year I’m 70 years old. I’m not a child anymore. I can’t work anymore. So it’s very difficult.

Voice
Residents like Hoffman say they’re very happy with the units they’ve received, but the fact that she still doesn’t have her title deed four years later is giving her sleepless nights.

Sound Up Alida
Derek: Alida, what would happen if you lost your home?

Alida: Yoh, it’s heartbroken (sic). Because all my pension money went in here… I don’t know Derek.

Link Derek
So what rights do the residents, who’ve already moved into the estate, and those people who’ve bought their units but now want their money back, have in terms of the law. Well it all boils down to the sales agreement.

Voice
Attorney Cilna Steyn specialises in property law.

Sound Up Cilna
Derek: You’ve looked at copies of some of the sales agreements, what are you comments?

Cilna: It is concerning. As a buyer, I would demand that my money be held in trust up to the point of transfer, but in terms of this particular agreement that is not a requirement.

Voice
The contracts do say that the units should be built within plus minus 6 months, but also say that buyers will have no claim against the developer should there be any delays.

Sound Up Cilna
Cilna: This is absolutely ridiculous, because the agreement doesn’t have a timeline requirement for the developer to build. And that’s the problem…there isn’t timelines where we can clearly say the developer is in breach, so we fall back to common law in this situation, but this does not feel right or look right in anyway.

Voice
And while the agreements do say the developer will transfer the units into buyers names, there is also no time limit given.

Sound Up Cilna
anything that happens where the developer does not perform in terms of this agreement will lead to lengthy, costly litigation in most cases.

Voice
But time and money are not commodities many pensioners, like Hendrik and Barbara Schutte who bought in Monarch last year, have endless supplies of.

Sound Up Hendrik
On a special price of R545 000, for a two bedroom place like this with granite tops, and appliances thrown in as a sweetener.

Voice
Schutte, who sufffers from an incurable lung disease, also says he paid the full amount upfront and agreed to rent one of the completed units in Monarch at R5000 a month while he waited for his home to be built. But 10 months down the line, he can’t afford the rent anymore and his home is nowhere to be seen.

Sound Up Hendrik
Hendrik: There’s five clusters of eight, before us, before they even start on the cluster where we are meant to be. And the pace at which the places are completed, I don’t see me and Barbara moving into a place of our own before my number is possibly up…

Barbara: And that’s a fact. You know this man’s just not playing the game, he’s just not playing the game.

Hendrik: You know my intention is to make sure that I’ve got my wife settled and sorted out in a place, before I go to the big garden.

Voice
A week after we’d asked Nico Venter for an on camera interview he still hadn’t agreed to a date, so we called him.

Sound Up Nico Venter Phone Call
Derek: That’s what we want to give you Nico is the right of reply.

Nico: No, not now. Not now.

Derek: Because we’ve spoken to elderly residents and buyers in tears, and would like to hear your side of the story.

Nico: That’s fine, I will let you know tomorrow when we can talk.

Derek: Would you also provide us with the documentation, proving that you have the rights to develop this land?
Nico: Yes.

Derek: You will?

Nico: Mmm.

Voice
But he didn’t get back to us the next day, and no documents were forthcoming. So we asked the Midvaal Municipality what the status of the development was. In a letter to Carte Blanche, they confirmed the following:

The property is zoned Residential 1 which does not permit for a retirement village
• There was a communication that the property should be rezoned to permit for the retirement village and such was never done
The conditions of the Site Development Plan were not complied with.
• The building plans were never submitted
A joint operation was conducted on the property and notices were issued in respect of all non-compliant buildings
• No Certificate of Occupation issued
• Certificate of acceptability and Health Permit not issued by Environmental Health
• and, No application submitted for the Sectional Title

Voice
Perhaps that’s why he seemed more concerned with us entering his property then with the plight of the people he’d sold homes to…

Nico: … you guys came on this site without me knowing.

Derek: We were invited onto the site by residents.

Nico: There’s boards all over the show that say you’ve got to report to me first.

Derek: I don’t think it’s in their sales agreement that they can’t have visitors.

Nico: You’re not a visitor, pleas let’s not fool around here.

Derek: Well there’s nothing in the sales agreement about you can’t invite the media?

Nico: I’m sorry, I beg to differ sir. But I’ll let you know tomorrow…

Derek: Nico, people have lost, you know their life savings…

Nico: Nobody has lost anything sir.

Derek: People have lost their life savings, why don’t you speak to us now?

Nico: I’m sorry, that’s not true, I said to you I will send my stuff through to you tomorrow, and thereafter we can sit…

Derek: But you know the story, you’ve been working on it for years, what have you got to research?

Nico: I don’t want this as being as an interview, I’ve said to you what I have to say, and I’ll let you know tomorrow.



Voice
Nico Venter asked us for more information before he would do an interview, but we’ve had no further response from him to our detailed list of questions or the letter from the municipality. As for the pensioners who paid over their life savings in good faith, they’ve been left in a precarious position, and it doesn’t look like they’ll be getting the title deeds to their homes anytime soon.

Sound Up Hendrik
You know its going to leave two 70 something year olds, with health problems both of them, with bloody nowhere to go.

Sound Up Simon
If he liquidates himself, or whatever, what foot have we got to stand on?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Years after paying in full for their houses, the elderly residents of a Retirement Village have acccused the developer of dodgy dealings, as their homes have not been registered in their names
metadata.Unique Selling Point: For the elderly residents of Monarch Eco Retirement Village, their retirement dreams have turned into a nightmare. Homeowners who bought properties in the village from as far back as 2016, say they are having sleepless nights as they are still not the registered owners of their properties. And they are now accusing the developer, Nico Venter, of fraud.
metadata.Summary: Except for their homes not being in their names, many of the residents woes started long before they could even move in. Case studies like Alida Hoffman and Simon Voort, who have agreed to on-camera interviews, both had to make alternative arrangements for accommodation when Nico's promises of delivering their new homes within 6 months of them paying for their units in full fell through. Simon had to rent a house for 15 months before he could move in. Other buyers have been left even worse off. Cobus du Preez paid a R450 000 deposit for his unit in 2019 - when building on his unit fell far behind schedule he refused to pay the remaining R100 000 of the R550 000 selling price until progress was made. Nico Venter cancelled the agreement, and has promised to refund Cobus but two years later du PReez has not seen his money back. But the really sad part is the absolute fear and uncertainty many of the elderly residents have - since the properties are not registered in their names, they cannot sell them, they cannot bequeath them to family, and none of them have the money or means to fight the case in court. NB I HAVE ASKED SPECIALIST PROPERTY ATTORNEYS SSLR TO LOOK AT THE CONTRACTS ETC. OWNER ATTORNEY CILNA STEYN (FROM A PREVIOUS HOUSE HIJACKINGS STORY) HAS AGREED TO DIG AROUND FOR US - SHE WILL GIVE ME A REPORT TOMORROW ON WHO OWNS THE PROPERTY WHERE THE ESTATE HAS BEEN BUILT, WHAT AGREEMENTS THERE WERE MADE AND IF THE DEVELOPMENT HAS BEEN REGISTERED LEGALLY ETC. SHE WILL ALSO DO AN ON CAMERA INTERVIEW REGARDING THE CONTRACTS AND RIGHTS OF THE BUYERS AND VENTER.

His wife owns five businesses, and has R86 million in various bank accounts. - Sergeant Kgapola from Brackenhurst SAPS has obtained a Section 205 for Venter's wife's banck accounts.
